chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Kahili, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a supplication: 'All praise is to Allah, the end of His Knowledge.' He wrote back to me: 'Do not say: the end of His Knowledge, but say: the end of His Pleasure.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (a title for Imam al-Rida or Imam al-Hadi depending on context, here referring to the Imam receiving the letter)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between 'end of knowledge' and 'end of pleasure' in Shia supplications?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) corrects the phrase 'the end of His Knowledge' to 'the end of His Pleasure' to avoid implying that divine knowledge has a limit or boundary, a concept often debated in Shia theology against the Mu'tazila. This distinction emphasizes that while God's pleasure is contingent upon human obedience and thus has a terminus, His knowledge is infinite and all-encompassing, preserving the attribute of *Sifat al-Ilm* as eternal and boundless.
